title: Cost Labyrinth: token-trace matrix and pricing pattern mapper for Console
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design a compact, queryable token-level cost matrix called 'Cost Labyrinth' to sit in the Redwood Console Cost views. The goal is to enable engineers and finance stakeholders to: 1) see per-token attribution for a selected time window and route, 2) compare pricing slab overlays (hosted vs dedicated vs quantized variants), and 3) export role-aware CSVs and sleeker JSON payloads for billing ingestion. This ticket covers the high-fidelity prototype, interaction spec, and a short usability pass with engineers + PMs. Key constraints: keep the UI dense for power users while supporting progressive disclosure for non-expert viewers.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma prototype of the token-trace matrix with adjustable granularity (per-token | per-segment | per-session).
Interaction spec describing hover details, drill-to-request, and timeline scrubbing.
Three export templates (compact CSV, role-aware CSV, JSON ledger) defined and linked to the export CTA.
PM and ENG have reviewed and left sign-off comments in Confluence; design moves to handoff with implementation notes.
Usability notes from a 5-person mixed PM/Eng/Finance session incorporated into the prototype.
decisions: Use a density slider (0-100%) to switch between token-dense and session-aggregated views rather than toggling discrete modes—minimizes context switch.
Show pricing-slab overlays as semi-transparent bands pinned to the timeline to allow side-by-side comparison of cost-per-token across model variants.
Default export is a role-aware CSV that includes role tags, inferred session ids, and an approximate cache-hit column. Advanced JSON ledger export is opt-in for billing integrations.
tradeoffs: Showing full per-token text with attribution increases cognitive load and width; we prioritize token position + cost and offer a hover card with full text to reduce horizontal space.

Real-time recomputation of exact per-token cost for long sessions is expensive. We show estimated per-token cost with an explicit confidence indicator and offer an on-demand recalculation for selected ranges.
Adding price-slab overlays increases visual complexity for novice users; we collapse slabs behind a toggle and provide a brief onboarding tooltip.
